text: dsh-browser-playwright-codex 是供 DSH Web 客户端使用的浏览器自动化插件：它把 Playwright 浏览器服务接入 DSH，并注册 browser_ 工具。主要功能包括打开网页、读取带稳定元素引用的页面快照、点击与填写表单、切换标签页和截取页面；持久浏览器配置可复用本地登录状态。适合让 agent 处理真实网页任务；无需额外 API key，浏览器及其配置需在本机可用。

dsh-browser-playwright-codex adds Playwright browser automation to DSH through browser_ tools. Agents navigate, inspect snapshots, click, fill forms, switch tabs, and capture screenshots. Persistent profiles reuse local sign-in state. It needs a local browser and no extra API key.

网页按钮不好定位时，有没有基于页面快照和元素引用的操作方式？
I want my DSH agent to navigate and interact with webpages in a browser.
Can an agent fill ordinary web forms and work across browser tabs?
I need page snapshots and screenshots for a browser-based workflow.
让 DSH 帮我从浏览器页面提取信息，方便继续处理任务。
dsh-browser-playwright-codex 的功能「导航」：插件提供 browser_navigate，让 agent 打开指定网页并取得页面结果；调用时输入目标 URL，结果供后续浏览器操作使用。
dsh-browser-playwright-codex 的功能「页面快照」：插件提供 browser_snapshot，读取当前页面的可访问内容并返回稳定元素引用；agent 可据此选择页面元素继续交互。
dsh-browser-playwright-codex 的功能「填写表单」：插件提供 browser_fill，根据页面快照中的元素引用填写普通文本输入；输入目标引用和值，凭据类字段会被拒绝。
dsh-browser-playwright-codex 的功能「标签页管理」：插件提供标签页列表、切换和新开等浏览器工具；agent 可查看当前标签并在页面间切换。
dsh-browser-playwright-codex 的功能「页面截图」：插件提供 browser_screenshot，将当前页面截图作为附件返回，供 DSH 会话查看。
dsh-browser-playwright-codex 使用本地持久浏览器配置保存会话登录状态；共享持久模式的不同调用会使用同一浏览器窗口与登录状态。见 cordis.patch.yml。

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · dsh-browser-playwright-codex：**In one line**: the agent drives a **visible, profile-backed browser window** with the logins you
already have — filling in forms, scraping lists and working across tabs in real pages — through
accessibility snapshots with stable element refs. Native dialogs are parked and reported instead of
auto-accepted. Challenge pages are detected and reported as a note that tells the agent to stop and hand
the page back — a note, not a block. There is **no sign-in detector**, and `browser_fill` refuses
password / one-time-code / card fields outright — you type those in the visible window. No
CSS-selector guessing, no full-DOM dumps.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · local development: clone, then link the checkout：**Compatibility.** Built and tested against DSH `0.2.0-rc.1`. The dependency ranges are **floors, not
wildcards**: peers `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `>=4.0.4`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` `>=0.2.0-rc.1`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` `>=0.2.0-rc.1`, and the direct dependency `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` `^3.18.4`. The
floors exist so an empty project cannot resolve a very old `0.0.1-rc.*` build, while a newer harness still
installs. One cost of npm's prerelease rules: a prerelease whose `[major, minor, patch]` tuple differs from
`0.2.0` (for example `0.2.1-rc.*`) is outside a `>=0.2.0-rc.1` range, so you may see a **peer warning** — a
warning, not an install failure (pnpm does not enforce peer ranges strictly by default). After a harness
upgrade, `npm run doctor` re-checks that every named export this plugin imports still exists — that is the
fast way to tell "the harness moved" from "the plugin broke".

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Your first task：Two habits worth having on day one:

- **Let it look before it clicks.** Start from `browser_snapshot`; a `ref` is only valid in the result that
  produced it (a stale one fails fast instead of clicking something else).
- **Say "stop" for the irreversible step.** Submitting, paying, deleting and sending are the points where
  you want to read the form first.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Browser binary：The provider probes `chromium` → `chrome` → `msedge` → `edge` channels automatically; any installed Chromium-family browser works with **zero download**. To use Playwright-managed Chromium instead:

```sh
npx playwright-core install chromium

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Restricted networks (e.g. mainland China):：PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST=https://cdn.npmmirror.com/binaries/playwright npx playwright-core install chromium
```

Or pin a binary: `launch.executablePath` / `launch.channel` in the plugin config.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Tools：The default `toolPrefix` is `browser_`. Every action returns a fresh snapshot, so refs always come from the latest result. The registered set is capability-gated: `browser_evaluate`, `browser_cdp` and `browser_extract` appear only when their capability is switched on (their schemas are resident in the system prompt on every turn, so a tool that could only answer "disabled" would be pure prompt cost). Count the live surface with `npm run cost` — the shipped `cordis.patch.yml` keeps **both power gates off** (since 0.4.7), so a profile mounting this bundle sees **16 tools**; 17 or 18 once your deployment opts into `evaluate` / `cdp`, 19 with `diagnostics: true`, 21 once `extract` is configured. How to opt in: paste the snippet under Known Limitations below, or use the built-in Settings card.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Tools：| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `browser_navigate` | Open a URL (http/https only) and return the snapshot |
| `browser_snapshot` | Snapshot the current page: URL, title, visible elements with `ref=` ids |
| `browser_click` | Click the target from the latest snapshot — a `ref`, a visible label the snapshot gave no ref (e.g. `{ text: "搜索设置" }`), or raw `x`/`y` viewport pixels as a last resort — or rest the pointer on it without activating anything with `mode: "hover"` (submenus, tooltips, previews, player controls); `precise: true` takes a ref click down the geometric-centre path. The returned snapshot opens with a landing note naming what received the click, and a dialog raised by a click stays pending — answer it with `browser_dialog` |
| `browser_fill` | Replace an input's value; selects match by option label |
| `browser_press` | Press a key (Enter, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown, …) on an element |
| `browser_scroll` | Scroll the page or bring a ref into view |
| `browser_back` / `browser_forward` | History navigation |
| `browser_wait` | Wait for one condition — an element, visible text, a quiet network — or a bounded duration; returns what it

The model then calls `browser_click` with `ref: e2`. Invisible content is excluded, node and text caps bound the token cost, and truncation is flagged in the result.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Result notes：A result can open with one or more notes before the tree. Each says what the plugin saw; none of them
claims to *prevent* anything:

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Result notes：- `[human verification]` — a challenge page was recognised; the line above the note names the tier
  (response header / widget / wording) and the evidence, and the note tells the agent to stop and ask
  you to finish it in the open window instead of retrying.
- `[http NNN]` — the main document answered a non-2xx status and no challenge was identified, so the
  tree may be an error page or an interception page rather than the content that was asked for.
- `[nothing here]` — the page has no clickable elements and almost no text: a gate or visitor check, a
  page that is still loading, or one that needs a person. The note says to take one more snapshot,
  then ask you rather than re-sending the same navigation.
- `[no visible change]` — the action left the page identical (after one action on a nearly empty page,
  or after two identical results on a page with content). It is worded as a guess on purpose: it is
  what an unrecognised wall looks like.
- A landing note (which element received the click), a parked-dialog note, and an engine-fallback note
  can also appear.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Result notes：An actionable element with no text of its own is named from its descendants — `搜索设置` renders as `link "搜索设置" [ref=e7]`, and `` as `link "图标链接" [ref=e8]` — so a visible label and the ref that carries it always appear on the same line. A non-actionable child that merely repeats an ancestor name is folded away, so each label appears once, on the line that carries the ref; container roles are never named from their content (a `

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Two levers that shrink what tools *return*：The resident schema cost is fixed, but two switches cut what each call sends back — useful on pages
whose snapshots are long, and both are off by default because both change what the model sees:
section: Two levers that shrink what tools *return*

text:
dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Two levers that shrink what tools *return*：- **`snapshot.diff`** (playwright row) — returns `+` / `-` / `~` diffs against the previous snapshot,
  keyed by stable refs, instead of the whole tree. A ref-nonce change is reported as a navigation reset,
  and a truncated tree falls back to the full snapshot, so the model is never handed a diff it cannot
  anchor. Turn it on when a page re-renders often and you resent paying for the same tree twice.
- **`interactiveOnlyDefault`** (tool row) — makes `browser_snapshot` default to actionable elements
  only; the model can still pass `interactiveOnly: false` per call when it needs the text around them.
  Frames are kept either way: an iframe's accessible name is the embedded widget's own title, which is
  how a challenge widget identifies itself, so pruning it would hide the wall the snapshot is meant to
  reveal.
section: Two levers that shrink what tools *return*

text:
dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Two levers that shrink what tools *return*：Both are honest trades, not free wins: a diff is smaller but requires the model to hold the previous
tree, and an interactive-only snapshot hides the prose the model may want to read. Measure before
turning them on in a deployment that shares prompts across many users.
section: Two levers that shrink what tools *return*

text: dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Window mode (headful / headless)：The Settings card has a **浏览器窗口** choice: show the window (headful, the default) or run it in the background (headless). The pick is stored in `~/.dsh/dsh-browser-playwright.state.json` and survives restarts; `launch.headless` stays the configured default for anyone who never picks.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Window mode (headful / headless)：Switching takes effect on the **next browser operation**: the provider compares the mode it launched with against the desired one and relaunches (login state is exported first, so the login survives; tabs and unsaved page state do not). Headless is honest about its cost — with no visible window, the “watch it and take over” guarantee for sign-ins and CAPTCHAs no longer holds, so use it only for unattended work where you accept that.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Cache and disk：The Settings card also carries a **缓存与磁盘** section: Chromium's pure caches inside the plugin's profile, `dsh-*` residue in `%TEMP%`, updater installers of the installed version, and the request-image cache are listed with their sizes; you preview first (“先预演”) and only then confirm. Cookies, Local Storage, Service Worker, IndexedDB, Network, Preferences and `~/.dsh/attachments` are never in scope — the target list is a closed enum in `src/cache-clean.ts`, and no path is ever taken from the request.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Prefer a switch to editing config?：The Settings card ships **inside this package** (it moved out of the companion package `dsh-browser-toggle`, which is retired) and puts
this on one card: enable/disable the browser, pick the page-reading mode, and turn the two
power tools on or off — no restart, no YAML. The card also lists **which sites this browser looks
signed in to**. Two things make that list trustworthy: cookies are attributed **first-party** — only
domains this browser actually visited are candidates, because a tracker's cookie belongs to the site
you were browsing, not to the tracker — and "looks signed in" follows OWASP's session-ID criteria
(an `HttpOnly` cookie *and* a session-scoped or token-shaped one), not cookie names or counts. Domains that belong to the same company collapse into **one row** (`京东系（18 个域）`) with the totals
for the whole family, expandable to the individual domains. Each row also says **what the site is** (`jinritemai.com` → 巨量千川（抖音电商广告后台）): the page's
own title when the browser has that domain open, otherwise a curated offline table, otherwise just the
domain — never a guess. It is
labelled as an inference rath

text:
dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Architecture：- `service` — `ctx.browser`: the provider registry with configured-or-auto selection semantics (a configured id must exist; one usable provider auto-selects; several require an explicit choice).
- `playwright` — the provider. **Persistent mode (default)**: one shared `launchPersistentContext` window on an independent profile directory (`~/.dsh/browser-profiles/playwright`), reused by every calling session — Codex-style personal browser. Login lives in the profile (durable cookies, localStorage) **plus** an exported state file (`dsh-storage-state.json`) that re-injects session cookies on relaunch (the browser drops those on close). The window auto-relaunches after an external close or crash, login intact. Set `launch.persistent: false` for the legacy shared-browser/per-owner-context mode — that mode writes **no** state file at all (the export is skipped rather than pointed at an empty path, which would have dropped cookie JSON into the process working directory). URL policy, idle disposal, and the injected snapshot engine apply to both.
- `tool` — the consumer: `defineTool`-built tools whose canonical values are structured JSON and

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Architecture：Other providers (remote browsers, Browserbase, Steel, …) can register into `ctx.browser`; the tool schemas stay unchanged. Browser sessions survive across tool calls; login state survives window close and harness restarts in persistent mode.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Test suites：The scenario suites are the plugin's most realistic tests: they drive the browser the way an agent does — snapshot, find a `ref`, act, re-snapshot — and therefore double as executable documentation of the model experience.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Test suites：From a DeepSeek Harness source checkout, the bundle layer to load is this repository's
[`cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/miqian-nomad/dsh-browser-playwright-codex/blob/main/cordis.patch.yml) — the
same file the package ships. Register the checkout through your profile with
`dsh plugin --profile <name> add link:<absolute path to this directory>` (above); this repository carries no
separate dev patch file.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Tool schemas：The tool schemas join the system-prompt assembly through `ctx.tools.register()`; each carries a one-line task-oriented description. The registered set is derived from `src/contract.ts` and checked against it at plugin load, so a renamed or forgotten tool fails loudly instead of silently vanishing from the model's view. Snapshot results are bounded: at most `maxNodes` nodes, names capped at `maxNameLength`, and the truncation flag is explicit.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Token effect：One tool schema block per tool (small, fixed), plus per-call result text proportional to the visible page, capped by ``snapshot.maxNodes`` and name/text limits. Actions return a fresh snapshot, so interactive flows cost roughly one snapshot per step.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · KV Cache effect：Tool schemas are static per registration and keep the prompt prefix stable. Result content varies with the page, invalidating reuse after each browser tool call, as with any tool result.

dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Persistent mode is one shared window** — all calling sessions drive the same profile-backed window and share its login state and tabs. Ideal for a personal assistant; if you need hard per-session isolation (separate logins per conversation), set `launch.persistent: false` and manage per-owner contexts, or run separate DSH profiles.
- **Headless servers must opt in** — the bundle defaults to `headless: false`; on a headless/remote host set `launch.headless: true`.
- **Selector-free, not vision-free** — interaction is a11y-tree based; purely visual widgets (canvas, WebGL, custom-drawn controls) may expose no refs. `browser_screenshot` + an image-capable model is the fallback.
- **Cross-origin iframes** appear as leaf `(frame)` nodes without refs; same-origin frames are walked up to two levels deep.
- **Evaluate gate is config, not approval** — enabling `allowEvaluate` trusts the model with arbitrary page JavaScript; compose it with the harness approval/permission policy for stricter control. dsh-browser-playwright-codex README · Ref and lifecycle safety (fixed)：- **Stale refs fail fast** — refs carry a per-snapshot nonce, so after a client-side re-render a stale ref matches nothing and `browser_click` fails with `REF_NOT_FOUND` instead of silently acting on a different element.
- **Link clicks respect `allowedDomains`** — every click path is checked before any input is delivered: `browser_click` — ref mode (the element's `href`), `precise` ref mode, and raw-coordinate mode (the enclosing link found at the point). A disallowed host is rejected with `URL_NOT_ALLOWED`. `javascript:` links are exempt because they run in-page and navigate nowhere; other non-http(s) schemes stay refused.
- **A page-opened tab outside `allowedDomains` cannot be driven** — two layers: the request-level guard refuses the popup's document (so it never loads the disallowed host), and `browser_switch_tab` still refuses to enter a tab that already sits on one (the current tab is kept).
- **Idle disposal defers during operations** — a navigation slower than `idleTimeoutMs` completes normally; disposal only fires when the session is truly idle.
